title: Microsoft Defender for Identity: unified identity timeline on the Identity page
summary: The roadmap facts, timeline details, licensing explanation and documented access controls check out. The assertion that remediation behaviour is unchanged is not established by the sources, and the checklist's identity-scoping control has no corresponding table row.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Scope: Access; Governance controls; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Unified RBAC custom roles and their data-source assignments control read access to Defender data, including Defender for Identity.
claims.quote: If you assigned read-only permissions for a single data source, such as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, the assigned users can't read alerts in the other services, such as Microsoft Defender for Office 365 or Microsoft Defender for Identity.

claims.where: Scope: Access; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Defender for Identity access can be scoped to Active Directory domains or organisational units.
claims.quote: When you configure the role, you choose which users or Entra ID groups can access specific Active Directory domains or organizational units.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Tenants with roles assigned or exported before March 2, 2025 retain their configuration.
claims.quote: Starting March 2, 2025, new Microsoft Defender for Identity tenants can only configure permissions through Microsoft Defender XDR Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Tenants with roles assigned or exported before this date will retain their current configuration.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The portal enforces configured unified RBAC permissions and assignments only after activation.
claims.quote: For the Microsoft Defender portal to start enforcing the permissions and assignments configured in your new or imported roles, you need to activate the new Microsoft Defender unified RBAC model.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating custom roles requires at least Security Administrator in Entra ID or all unified RBAC Authorization permissions.
claims.quote: To create custom roles in Microsoft Defender unified RBAC, you must be assigned one of the following roles or permissions: At leastSecurity Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID. All Authorization permissions assigned in Microsoft Defender Unified RBAC.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: POST /beta/roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments creates a Defender role assignment.
claims.quote: Example 4: Create a role assignment in Defender over all and future workloads, in scope of CloudSet '123': ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The request body uses appScopeIds, with Mdi a workload ID.
claims.quote: To allow assignments over workload, on all scopes, don't add any scope after the following workload IDs in appScopeIds: Mdi, Mdc, Mda, Mde, Mdo, SecureScoreExternal.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Graph call uses beta, whose APIs Microsoft says are subject to change.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Custom scoped roles apply only to new alerts and activities, not retroactively to those triggered before the role was created.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Overview page's Actions menu triggers remediation actions such as disabling accounts and revoking sessions.
claims.quote: From the Overview page, use the Actions menu to trigger remediation actions on the identity. ... Available actions can include disabling or enabling accounts, revoking sessions

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: There is no change to autonomy and actions from the timeline update.
claims.quote: Searched: identity Timeline tab Actions menu remediation no change unified timeline. Read roadmap, investigate-users and remediation-actions search excerpts; they describe the view and action mechanisms but do not establish unchanged behaviour before and after this update.
claims.fix: Remove 'No change:' from the Autonomy & actions bullet. Retain the documented description of the Timeline tab and the Overview Actions menu.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks the reader to check has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check the data sources and Defender for Identity scopes in each unified RBAC assignment.' Table: role and data-source assignment, and tenant-wide timeline switch; no identity-scoping row.
claims.fix: Remove 'and Defender for Identity scopes' from the Before rollout checklist bullet so it asks only to check data sources in each unified RBAC assignment. The identity-scoping check has no table row.
